subject: Price the GC itself: suppress zero-yield maintenance under scarcity

body.new_observation: Repeated aggressive-reclaim cycles at roughly 1.95-2.98 GiB free are deleting only tens of KiB or nothing while still scanning and writing individual proof files. The maintenance path can therefore consume I/O, metadata writes, and CPU for less recovered capacity than its own operating cost.
policy_upgrade: Before each reclaim sweep, estimate expected_reclaim_bytes, scan_cost, proof_write_bytes, and rebuild_cost from the last inventory plus changed roots.

If expected_reclaim_bytes is below a configurable minimum useful yield OR reclaimed_bytes/proof_bytes from the previous sweep is below the efficiency floor, suppress the leaf sweep for a backoff window and emit gc_state=yield_exhausted.

Invalidate the backoff early only when ResourceGraph observes a large new candidate class, Docker state changes, a worker exits and releases ephemeral state, or physical free drops through an emergency floor.
Cache inventory by root fingerprint so unchanged trees are not rescanned every maintenance tick.
Never count already-deleted/recreated tiny caches as fresh strategic inventory; repeated regeneration should raise their rebuild-churn cost and lower their reclaim priority.
Under gc_state=yield_exhausted, spend the maintenance slot on low-write provider/parser/mesh/PartnerGraph repairs instead of another zero-yield walk.
